title: Security Engineering Weekly Sync — 2026-03-10
content:
Attendees: Ava Chen, Marcus Rivera, Priya Patel, Omar Haddad, Leah Brooks (joined late), Barnaby Wu (notes from triage), + SRE on call (via Slack).

Goals for today:
- Quick vulnerability triage for newly reported findings from internal scan and Contractor pen test.
- Review current secrets scanning false positives and decide on short-term filter updates.
- Threat model walkthrough for Admin Proxy feature (private deployments).
- Allocate action items and owners; ensure follow-ups scheduled.

1) Vulnerability triage (15m)
- Source: Internal weekly dependency scan (Snyk) + contractor pen test report v1.1.
- High-level: 3 medium CVEs flagged in common libs (graphql-java, okhttp), 1 low-finding in frontend deps, and 1 application logic issue flagged by contractor (auth check bypass proof-of-concept).

Findings summary:
- SEC-482 (internal): graphql-java CVE-2025-XXXX — severity: medium. Affects our ingestion pipeline (model metadata parser). Exploitability: limited (requires crafted schema payload).
  - Decision: patch priority P2. Marcus to schedule a patch PR against infra/common-modeling by 2026-03-15, include unit test verifying strict schema parsing. If patch unavailable upstream within 7 days, apply a temporary runtime input sanitizer in the service layer (append WAF rule).

- SEC-487: okhttp (CVE-2026-YYY) — severity: medium. Affects ramping Dedicated capacity heartbeat client. Exploitability: low on our config due to TLS and client settings, but public exploit PoC exists.
  - Decision: upgrade okhttp in gateway image to 4.11.2 ASAP. Omar to prototype upgrade in staging today and run canary for heartbeats. Target deploy: 2026-03-18. Add monitoring alert for increased connect failures post-upgrade.

- Contractor finding: auth check bypass on Admin Proxy when X-Forwarded-User header present and behind specific LB config. Proof-of-concept attached in linked_artifacts (Contractor report). Severity: high if externally reachable, currently mitigated by internal LB configs and private deployment network rules.
  - Decision: treat as P1 until confirmed safe. Action: Priya to reproduce PoC against a dedicated staging private deployment by 2026-03-12, validate if header sanitation occurs at edge. If repro succeeds, immediate hardshell: drop headers at LB and add explicit header validation in Admin Proxy (code PR). Also open incident-runbook draft.

- Low frontend deps: defer to FE team; Leah to drop owners a note.

Notes/Context:
- We intentionally run some older minor versions for stability in Dedicated, but need clear tech-debt tickets. Add to roadmap: 'dep-hardening' epic.

2) Secrets scanning (20m)
- Recent scan on main repo surfaced 2 suspected tokens in historical commits (candidate tokens masked in report). Both appear to be service tokens generated for an internal sandbox and rotated 2025-11; no active usage found via audit logs.
  - Action: Barnaby to run credential usage check across logs and revoke any lingering tokens by 2026-03-12. Update secrets-scan ignore rules to reduce false positives for ephemeral sandbox names (pattern: sandbox-.*-tmp).

- False positives: several AWS ARNs and k8s serviceaccount names flagged; these are not secrets. We need better pattern tuning. Decision: update regex whitelist and re-run full repo-scan next week. Marcus + Priya to own regex update by 2026-03-13.

- Secrets rotation policy reminder: Quarterly rotation for high-privileged service tokens; monthly for CI runner credentials. Leah to draft short note to infra team about enforcing rotation for self-hosted runners (status: in_progress, due 2026-03-20).

- Short-term detection improvement: Add rule to detect long-lived PATs and alert on creation. Tie alert to onboarding flow for new repos (add to onboarding checklist).

3) Threat modeling: Admin Proxy (private deployments) (25m)
- Background: Admin Proxy exposes management endpoints for customer private deployments (VPC/on-prem). We need to ensure administrative surfaces cannot be abused when routing changes or when customers integrate custom LB configs.

Walkthrough notes:
- Trust boundaries: public redwood control plane -> private control plane -> Admin Proxy -> customer VPC systems.
- Assets: admin API tokens, cluster-level credentials, customer secrets (KMS metadata), audit logs.
- Entry points: config UI, API routes, health-check endpoints, websocket management channels.

Threats highlighted:
- Header spoofing (X-Forwarded-User / X-Admin-Auth) if LB misconfigured — mitigations: canonicalize and strip inbound headers at edge, verify mTLS where possible, runtime header allowlist.
- Replay of management commands — mitigations: nonce/timestamp checks, short-lived management tokens, strict RBAC.
- Unauthorized lateral movement from compromised customer VPC to admin plane — mitigations: network segmentation, IP allowlists, strict egress filtering on admin agents.
- Secret exposure in logs — mitigations: structured logging with secret redaction (mask KMS keys, tokens), log scrubbing pipeline.

Decisions and next steps:
- Implement header stripping at LB for all private deployment customers by default. (Omar + Infra) Target: 2026-03-24. Add toggles to allow explicit passthrough only with documented risk acceptance.
- Add mTLS support for Admin Proxy control plane by default; pilot with 2 customers next month. (Priya) Proposal doc due 2026-03-20.
- Create a design doc for short-lived admin tokens with rotation + nonces. (Ava) Draft due 2026-03-17.
- Threat model documented in Confluence (linked_artifacts). Priya + Ava to update with diagrams and attach attack trees.

4) Observability & detection updates (10m)
- Current SOC rule for 'suspicious-admin-login' needs tuning — recent spike due to scheduled maintenance. Action: Leah to add suppression window for scheduled maintenance JQL tags.
- Add rule to detect new repo-level PAT creation outside normal onboarding flow. Marcus to implement detection and alert to #sec-notify.

5) Action Items (consolidated)
- Marcus: Patch graphql-java and update dependency epic ticket (SEC-482). PR by 2026-03-15.
- Omar: Okhttp upgrade prototype + heartbeat canary in staging. Deploy target 2026-03-18. LB header-stripping implementation plan by 2026-03-17.
- Priya: Reproduce Admin Proxy auth bypass PoC in staging by 2026-03-12; mTLS proposal doc by 2026-03-20.
- Barnaby: Secrets usage check and rotation for sandbox tokens; revoke if active by 2026-03-12.
- Leah: Draft infra note on runner rotation and adjust SOC suppression windows. Due 2026-03-20.
- Ava: Design doc for short-lived admin tokens with nonce flow. Draft 2026-03-17.
- Marcus + Priya: Update secrets-scan regex whitelist by 2026-03-13.

Open questions / Parking lot:
- Clarify whether Dedicated heartbeat clients are exposed to customer networks in some edge cases (Marcus to confirm with Dedicated team).
- Do we want to require customer-permitted mTLS for all private deployments or provide as opt-in? (Decision slated for next sync after pilot results).
- Do we need a hardened build variant with ASLR/PIE flags for Admin Proxy binary? Security wants to discuss with release-engineering.

Notes to self / informal:
- Reproduce contractor PoC asap — contractor deadlines push for a faster turnaround.
- Watch for increased noise after okhttp upgrade — ensure rollback plan is clean and metrics tagged.

Meeting adjourned. Next sync: 2026-03-17 10:00 PT.

Attachments / References:
- Contractor report (link in linked_artifacts).
- Snyk weekly export (internal).
- Draft incident runbook template (confluence:sec/incident-runbooks).

End of notes.
